claude.sample_unit: simulated records (10,000 per noise level) based on 714 SMOTE-balanced Wisconsin Breast Cancer records
models_evaluated: one-class support vector machine (RBF kernel, nu=0.01)

links.outcome: Share of simulated drifted records flagged as outliers versus inliers by OCSVM at three noise levels
links.effect: Records misclassified as inliers: 27/10,000 (0.27%) at 5% noise, 486 (4.86%) at 10%, 851 (8.51%) at 30%. Most drifted records were flagged, but detection fell as overlap with training data grew.
links.quote: At the lowest noise level (5%), the model classified 27 records as inliers (27 out of 10,000).

links.outcome: Ability of unsupervised OCSVM monitor to detect simulated input population drift without ground-truth labels
links.effect: Sensitivity to drift decreased as overlap increased: inliers 27 (5% noise), 486 (10%), 851 (30%) of 10,000 each. Proof of concept on simulated data only.
links.quote: We hypothesised that increased noise would correlate with more OCSVM-detected inliers, indicating a sensitivity to population drift.

unlisted_practices: Using a one-class SVM trained on the original training data as an unsupervised, label-free detector of population drift on individual patient records

links.effect: Inliers among drifted records: 27/10,000 at 5% noise, 486/10,000 at 10%, and 851/10,000 at 30%.
